svg.title: AGV drive kinematics – differential, tricycle, mecanum (example values)
svg.text: Drive kinematics – what the navigation PC must calculate every cycle (10 ms)
Top views, driving direction ▲ (x forward, y to the left, ω positive = turn left). Example numbers from guide 11 §19 – verified with Python.
v_R = v + ω·b/2 , v_L = v − ω·b/2
Example: v 0.6 m/s on R 1.0 m → ω 0.6 rad/s
= 1864 / 1192 rpm at the motor (2546 rpm per m/s)
Turn on the spot: v = 0, v_R = −v_L = ω·b/2
R = L / tan δ = 1.559 m (not to scale)
Example: v_s 0.6 m/s, δ 30°, L 0.9 m
δ = 85° → R 0.079 m (almost on the spot,
turns about the rear axle centre)
− large swept area, no sideways move
+ moves sideways and diagonal, turns on the spot,
very small aisles, exact docking without manoeuvre
− rollers need a clean, flat, hard floor; low efficiency
sideways; slip → worse odometry; joints/steps hurt;
Choosing the drive concept (rule of thumb)
Dual steer-drive: each unit i at (x_i, y_i): v_ix = v_x − ω·y_i, v_iy = v_y + ω·x_i, steering angle = atan2(v_iy, v_ix), wheel speed = √(v_ix² + v_iy²).
Example: units at x = ±0.6 m, v_x 0.5, v_y 0.2 m/s, ω 0.3 rad/s → front unit 0.628 m/s at 37.2°, rear unit 0.500 m/s at 2.3°.
Omni 3-wheel (wheels at 90°/210°/330°, R 0.25 m): v_i = −sin θ_i · v_x + cos θ_i · v_y + R · ω → v_x 0.4 m/s gives −0.4 / +0.2 / +0.2 m/s.
